findings.assertion: The urban response to the September 1847 occupation is a distinct subject of historical investigation: Luis Fernando Granados devoted a 1999 UNAM history thesis to an uprising in Mexico City on 14–16 September, after the main 13 September assault at Chapultepec. The thesis title establishes the period and scope of the scholarly study, not exact street-by-street events or casualty figures.
findings.source_locator: UNAM 1999 thesis descriptive title and date; ELEM 2003 edition summary; existing INAH September 13 Chapultepec source
findings.limitations: Full thesis and original occupation records not yet examined; differentiation between military capitulation and later civilian actions is a research framing; do not infer participants' identities, motives or exact routes

findings.assertion: The 2003 edition description of Granados's Sueñan las piedras presents the September 1847 resistance as numerous actions by common residents, set amid the social geography of Mexico City's neighborhoods and streets. This is a description of the author's published interpretation, not independent proof of each reported action.
findings.source_locator: ELEM entry, back-cover excerpt supplied by publisher, 2003 edition
findings.limitations: Publisher back-cover copy only; do not cite particular Alameda or Santo Domingo incidents until book passages and their documentary footnotes are inspected

findings.assertion: The Library of Congress catalogs a lithograph issued by N. Currier in 1847 under a title assigning the storming of Chapultepec to 12 September 1847. INAH's separate chronology distinguishes bombardment beginning 12 September from the 13 September assault. The lithograph's printed title is evidence of contemporary visual representation, not independently reliable proof of the assault's day.
findings.source_locator: LOC item 2001706295 catalog title and c1847 attribution; prior INAH 2024 Chapultepec institutional account, first two battle paragraphs
findings.limitations: LOC item page inaccessible direct; image inscription and artist claim not visually checked. No rights clearance granted merely by identifying an image; crosscheck actual artifact and military documents before a visual caption

findings.assertion: Universidad Iberoamericana's Actas de Cabildo collection lists a digitized 1847 Ayuntamiento de la Ciudad de México volume, providing a candidate primary documentary series for testing municipal decisions and responses around the September occupation. The catalog proves the collection exists; it does not establish what the actas say about the uprising.
findings.source_locator: Actas de Cabildo, 1847 catalog record, downloadable RTF and PDF links
findings.limitations: No 1847 council text read or paginated. This is a documentary source-discovery finding only; not a claim about a particular vote or policy
